angle_en: All sacrifices are born of action

en.intro: Krishna gathers all the sacrifices he has taught and points to their common source.
en.notice: The key is that every sacrifice is a karma. When Arjuna sees that even sacred ritual belongs to the realm of action, he stops clinging to the results of any ritual.
en.next: Krishna now turns to the sacrifice of pure knowledge, declaring it greater than any material offering.
en.meaning: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने जो भी यज्ञ सिखाए, उन सबको एक साथ लाते हैं और उनकी एक साझा उत्पत्ति की ओर इशारा करते हैं।
hi.meaning: इस प्रकार और भी बहुत तरह के यज्ञ वेद की वाणी में विस्तार से कहे गए हैं। उन सब यज्ञों को तू कर्मजन्य जान। इस प्रकार जानकर यज्ञ करने से तू कर्मबन्धन से मुक्त हो जाएगा।
hi.notice: यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि हर यज्ञ एक कर्म है। जब अर्जुन देखते हैं कि पवित्र अनुष्ठान भी कर्म के ही दायरे में आते हैं, तो वे किसी भी कर्मफल से मोह छोड़ देते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब ज्ञान के यज्ञ की ओर मुड़ते हैं, और इसे भौतिक वस्तुओं के यज्ञ से श्रेष्ठ बताते हैं।

en.intro: Krishna gathers all the sacrifices he has taught and points to their common source.
en.body: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action. The key is that every sacrifice is a karma. When Arjuna sees that even sacred ritual belongs to the realm of action, he stops clinging to the results of any ritual. Krishna now turns to the sacrifice of pure knowledge, declaring it greater than any material offering.

meaning_changed: "कृष्ण अब सब कुछ एक साथ लाते हैं और उस एक बात की ओर इशारा करते हैं जो सबमें मौजूद है।" (The intro states that Krishna points to 'the one thing present in everything' (उस एक बात की ओर इशारा करते हैं जो सबमें मौजूद है). However, the verse itself does not mention a single unifying thing, but rather that all sacrifices are born of action and that knowledge of this frees one from bondage. This intro misrepresents the specific content of the verse by introducing a vague unifying concept.)
